_comment: **Every visual colour is stated, and stated as the nether's**, which is the world this type restates. An attribute a dimension type says nothing about falls back to its *registered* default, and for these three that default is #000000 — so an unstated colour is not a question handed to the biome, it is black. A biome overrides where it declares one and most do not: plains and beach carry no fog colour. `fog_color` and `sky_color` were left out on the reasoning that biomes carry their own, and every Age came up with black fog at every height over every landform (Jonah, 2026-09-03); `ambient_light_color` had already been caught the same way once. `ambient_light` is a separate system and is not the one you can see: it reaches only `LevelReader.getBrightness`, where the lightmap is built from `ambient_light_color`, `sky_light_color` and `sky_light_factor`. **`cardinal_light` was tried here and dropped** (Jonah, 2026-09-09, walked: "I cannot tell a difference"). It is a third axis and a real one -- a per-FACE multiplier applied at mesh time, the only one of the three that varies by which way a face points, and the nether's flattens the underside from 0.5 to 0.9. The reasoning was that it is what stops a roofed world reading as a cave with the lights off. Against a lightless Age that is not roofed, it is not visible, so it is not carried: a field nobody can see is a field to explain away later. `notes/coloured-light-research.md` keeps how it works, for whoever wants it for something the eye can actually catch.
